verses.text: These are the nations the LORD left in the land to test the Israelites who had not been through any of the wars in Canaan.
He did this only to teach war to the new generations of Israelites who had never fought in battle before.
These nations were the five rulers of the Philistines, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites living in the Lebanon mountains from Mount Baal Hermon to Lebo Hamath.
They were left to test the Israelites, to see whether they would obey the commands the LORD had given their ancestors through Moses.
The Israelites lived among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites.
They married their daughters and gave their own daughters to their sons, and they served their gods.
The Israelites did what was evil in the LORD's eyes. They forgot the LORD their God and served the Baals and the Asherah poles.
So the LORD was angry with Israel and sold them to Cushan-Rishathaim, king of Aram Naharaim in Mesopotamia. The Israelites served him for eight years.
But when they cried out to the LORD, he raised up someone to save them: Othniel son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother.
The Spirit of the LORD came on him, and he became Israel's judge and went to war. The LORD gave Cushan-Rishathaim king of Aram into his hands, and Othniel defeated him.
So the land had peace for forty years, until Othniel son of Kenaz died.
Again the Israelites did evil in the LORD's eyes. Because they did this evil, the LORD made Eglon king of Moab strong against Israel.
Eglon got the Ammonites and Amalekites to join him. He came and attacked Israel, and they captured the City of Palm Trees.
The Israelites served Eglon king of Moab for eighteen years.

Again the Israelites cried out to the LORD, and he gave them a saviour: Ehud son of Gera from the tribe of Benjamin, a left-handed man. The Israelites sent him to take their tribute payment to Eglon king of Moab.
Ehud had made a double-edged sword about half a metre long. He strapped it to his right thigh under his clothes.
He gave the tribute to Eglon king of Moab, who was a very fat man.
After Ehud had handed over the tribute, he sent away the men who had carried it.
But near the stone idols at Gilgal he turned back and said, "Your Majesty, I have a secret message for you." The king said, "Quiet!" and all his servants left the room.
Ehud went up to him while he was sitting alone in the cool upstairs room of his palace. Ehud said, "I have a message from God for you." As the king got up from his seat,
Ehud reached with his left hand, pulled the sword from his right thigh and pushed it into the king's belly.
Even the handle went in after the blade, and the fat closed over it. Ehud did not pull the sword out, and it came out at his back.
Then Ehud went out to the porch. He shut the doors of the upstairs room behind him and locked them.
After he had gone, the servants came and found the doors of the upstairs room locked. They said, "He must be relieving himself in the inner room."
They waited until they were embarrassed, but he still did not open the doors. So they took a key and unlocked them. There lay their master on the floor, dead.
While they were waiting, Ehud escaped. He passed by the stone idols and escaped to Seirah.
When he arrived, he blew a trumpet in the hill country of Ephraim, and the Israelites came down with him from the hills, with Ehud leading them.

He told them, "Follow me, because the LORD has given your enemy Moab into your hands." So they followed him down and took control of the river crossings of the Jordan leading to Moab. They did not let anyone cross over.
At that time they killed about ten thousand Moabites, all of them strong and brave fighters. Not one escaped.
That day Moab was put under Israel's control, and the land had peace for eighty years.
After Ehud came Shamgar son of Anath, who killed six hundred Philistines with an ox stick. He too saved Israel.
